underway:
Six Magic Outcome Notes are scheduled on Substack, as reported by Muxin. Live publication has not been verified here.
An existing Substack and LinkedIn content backlog is available to reuse.
Human Inference already has essays, newsletter signup and a subscriber survey.
testing:
Magic Outcome hypotheses: overwhelm to agency, despair to hope, and outrage to joyful creation.
Which audience needs resonate, which platforms reach those readers, and which content leads to meaningful action? Substack is not assumed to be the best platform.
next:
Connect the existing six Notes to the hypotheses and evidence we want to learn from.
Propose a bounded set of additional platforms and suitable content adaptations for review, using Content Studio instead of starting from zero.
gaps:
Establish the baseline and attribution for essay visits, newsletter signups and survey responses. These are existing funnel stages, but their measurements are not established in this Venture record.
The paid offer remains deliberately open. Requests, leads and sales are future stages, not missing interview answers.
constraints:
No employees to manage.
No more than 30 work hours per week; most Fridays completely off.
No more than two meetings per day, each at most 45 minutes.
No work interrupting evenings or weekends with family.
Content work fits the smaller stated budget of a few hours per week, up to eight if needed. Writing is the natural medium.
Prefer income from created products and writing, not client management. Platform testing must fit this workload.
